newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power flat to lower amid weaker natgas.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power flat to lower amid weaker natgas.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) finished Friday flat to lower versus Thursday's levels along with weaker natural gas prices, market sources said.
Swing natgas prices for the weekend along the Texas Gulf Coast were assessed at $2.24-$2.29 per million British thermal units, down from Thursday's $2.33-$2.38 for Friday delivery.
In addition to lower fuel costs, modest power demand in the ERCOT region also depressed physical prices, traders said.

Lower Colorado River Authority will shut its 430 megawatt (MW) natural gas-fired Ferguson power plant later today to repair a leaking boiler tube. The outage of the Marble Falls, Tx., plant was scheduled to last five days.
Peak, firm electricity in ERCOT for Monday was quoted near $20.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), compared with Thursday's range of $20.00-$22.00.
ERCOT electricity for delivery in 16-hour blocks over the five business days next week was still assessed at $20.00-$21.50.
November ERCOT electricity was quoted at $19.85-$20.00, down slightly from Thursday's quote of $20.25.
December ERCOT power was pegged at $21.00-$22.00, a wider range than Thursday's $21.50-$21.75.
